name: Djerba Zarzis International Airport
before:
The airport for Djerba, and an important arrival point for seasonal leisure flights to the island.

It is older than most Tunisian resort airports, dating from 1950 when it opened as Djerba Mellita. It was enlarged and renamed Djerba Zarzis International in 1970.

Because the traffic is largely seasonal, check what is actually flying for a client's dates rather than assuming a year round schedule.
after:
Djerba-Zarzis is the airport for Djerba, and an important arrival point for seasonal flights.

Because some routes run only in season, check what is actually flying for a client's dates rather than assuming a year round schedule.

claims.claim: Djerba-Zarzis is the airport for Djerba
claims.inAfter: Djerba-Zarzis is the airport for Djerba
claims.note: The old text opened 'The airport for Djerba'. The name comes from the renaming sentence, which is cut for its dates (below); OACA's figures, Tunisair Express and Wikipedia all write it Djerba-Zarzis, and Tunisair Express gives its address as Djerba's international airport. City Served is blank on the record.

sources.org: Mosaique FM (Tunisian radio, reporting an OACA communiqué)

sources.quote: is an international airport serving the island of Djerba in Tunisia

claims.claim: an important arrival point for seasonal flights
claims.inAfter: and an important arrival point for seasonal flights.
claims.note: Was 'seasonal leisure flights to the island'. Important: OACA's 2024 figures give Djerba-Zarzis 2,203,957 passengers, up 12.8 per cent, second only to Tunis-Carthage among the airports OACA runs. Seasonal: Nouvelair's new Djerba to Nice flights run from 15 June to 14 September 2026, and Transavia's Montpellier to Djerba flights, 'une route saisonnière', run to 18 October 2026 (Destination Tunisie). 'Leisure' and 'to the island' are dropped: beyond Wikipedia, only an unofficial guide site says them.

sources.org: Mosaique FM (Tunisian radio, reporting an OACA communiqué)
quote: le trafic sur l'aéroport Djerba-Zarzis a augmenté de 12.8% avec un nombre total de 2.203.957 passagers reçus
l'Aéroport Tunis-Carthage a accueilli un nombre record de passagers qui s'établit à 7.249.701
A compter du 15 juin, deux fréquences par semaine les lundis et vendredis jusqu'au 14 septembre 2026.
Tous les lundis jusqu'au 18 octobre 2026, Transavia opèrera sur la ligne Montpellier-Djerba

sources.quote: Today, it is an important destination for seasonal leisure flights.

claims.claim: some routes run only in season
claims.inAfter: Because some routes run only in season
claims.note: Was 'Because the traffic is largely seasonal'. No monthly traffic figures for Djerba could be read (OACA's site did not connect), so the text says what the route announcements show: seasonal routes such as Nouvelair's Djerba to Nice (15 June to 14 September 2026) and Transavia's Montpellier to Djerba (to 18 October 2026).

quote: A compter du 15 juin, deux fréquences par semaine les lundis et vendredis jusqu'au 14 septembre 2026.

claims.claim: seasonal leisure flights to the island
claims.wasBefore: an important arrival point for seasonal leisure flights to the island
claims.why: 'Leisure' and 'to the island' rest on Wikipedia and on djerbaairport.net, an unofficial guide site (it sells hotels and speaks of OACA in the third person), which is not a second source. Softened (above).

claims.claim: older than most Tunisian resort airports, opened in 1950 as Djerba Mellita
claims.wasBefore: It is older than most Tunisian resort airports, dating from 1950 when it opened as Djerba Mellita.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and disputed: the unofficial djerbaairport.net says the airport started serving in 1970. OACA, the operator, could not be reached (oaca.nat.tn failed to connect when tried for Tunis, one try). The comparison with other resort airports would need their opening dates as well.

sources.org: djerbaairport.net (an unofficial airport guide that sells hotels; not the operator)
sources.quote: Airport started serving in 1970 to bring tourists directly to the Djerba Island.

claims.claim: enlarged and renamed Djerba Zarzis International in 1970
claims.wasBefore: It was enlarged and renamed Djerba Zarzis International in 1970.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone for the enlargement and the renaming date (the unofficial guide site has 1970 as the start of service instead). The name itself is kept (above).

claims.wasBefore: Because the traffic is largely seasonal
claims.why: No monthly traffic figures could be read to show how much of the year is seasonal. Softened to the seasonal routes the sources name (above).

Held back: a new fact that replaces nothing (the old text gave no traffic figure). OACA's 2024 figure, reported by Mosaique FM on 5 January 2025, matches the Wikipedia infobox. No 2025 figure was found.

sources.org: Mosaique FM (Tunisian radio, reporting an OACA communiqué)
sources.quote: le trafic sur l'aéroport Djerba-Zarzis a augmenté de 12.8% avec un nombre total de 2.203.957 passagers reçus

claims.claim: FCDO advice on the Libyan border area, which excludes Zarzis
claims.why: Held back: a warning that replaces nothing, but the one Andy may want here. The FCDO advises against all travel to the town of Ben Guerdane and its surroundings and within 20 km of the Libyan border north of Dhehiba, and against all but essential travel within 75 km of the border, excluding Zarzis, the C118 road and all areas of Medenine Governorate north of that road (updated 24 July 2026, still current 23 September 2026). Djerba is not named in the advice.

sources.org: UK FCDO (Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office)
quote: the town of Ben Guerdane and immediate surrounding area
within 20km of the rest of the Tunisia-Libya border area north of Dhehiba

In addition, FCDO advises against all but essential travel to within 75km of the Tunisia-Libya border, including Remada and El Borma but excluding Zarzis, the C118 road and all areas in Medenine Governorate north of the road.

opinion.why: The old text's advice, kept: the named seasonal routes stop in September and October.
